requestedBy: Simon's standing 2026-10-06 instruction to keep pushing the prompt line until it beats main's text on the frozen corpus, and the recorded escalation in config/frontier-harness-preservation-pair-20261006.json#outcome.escalation, which asked for a second paired sample so the window term can be estimated with n=2 before any criterion decision is taken.
whatThisIs: The second same-window paired sample of two already-frozen texts. It measures nothing new about any candidate: both texts were measured in the first pair (candidate 2.21.0 read 19, control 2.11.0 read 18) and the control text also read 21 in the 2026-10-05 window. Its only purpose is to give the pending criterion decision a second estimate of (a) the window term - the same text measured in two windows - and (b) the candidate-minus-control difference in a fresh window. It is not a retry of a failed reading and it is not expected or permitted to produce a win: no cell is re-run to change an existing verdict, and no earlier reading or decision is replaced, revised or reinterpreted by anything measured here.
iterationDisclosure: This is sample 2 of the same pair, not a fifth prompt variant. The candidate text is byte-for-byte the text measured in sample 1 (6,165 bytes / e85b985e…, best-agent 48e8aa64) and the control text is byte-for-byte main's (6,014 bytes / cc23fe7a…). The corpus is a diagnostic set here, not a holdout: every earlier verdict of every cell stays published and nothing measured here replaces it. The texts are re-dispatched only because one attempt per cell cannot separate a one-to-three-cell difference from window and infrastructure variance, which is exactly the question the escalation left to the human.
question: At one frozen profile (deepseek-v4-flash, reasoning effort max) over the frozen 30-task frontier-harness corpus, how many of the 30 predeclared tasks do the two frozen texts pass when both are measured in one fresh window - the candidate 2.21.0 (main's 6,014-byte instruction plus the 2.15.0 preservation sentence) and main's 2.11.0 text itself - so that the window term and the candidate-minus-control difference each have a second observation?

readingPlan: Bind each arm: run headSha equals its own ref commit; every cell's first-request Skill instruction matches the arm's frozen bytes and SHA-256 (candidate 6,165 / e85b985e…, control 6,014 / cc23fe7a…); every record agrees on one candidate id; candidate.single / provider.single / instructions.frozen intact, provider.reasoningEffort=max, coverage.full passed.
Tabulate per cell per arm: disposition, reward, f2p/p2p, terminal cause, duration against budget, call count, deliverable presence on the two graded paths, upstream-fetch signature.

Report each arm's pass count beside the frozen reference (21) and beside sample 1, and report the window term as the control text's three readings (21 / 18 / this sample) rather than choosing among them.
Write the outcome into this file's outcome section, commit and push to codex/prompt-preservation-execution.

This sample never merges anything by itself and never satisfies or fails the merge gate on its own: the gate and the criterion remain exactly as the first pair predeclared them until the human decides.
Do not take a third sample after this one: n=2 is the predeclared depth of the window-variance estimate.
fairnessDisclosures: No user prefix, no task-specific hint, no grader output and no evaluator feedback reaches either arm; the texts are byte-identical to sample 1's.
One attempt per cell per arm; no best-of-N, no retry-until-pass, no cell exclusion, no latency threshold, no cell dropped for being slow.
Both arms are dispatched from their own frozen refs; neither ref is moved after dispatch.
Nothing measured here replaces any earlier verdict, and the sample is not used to select the more favourable of the two windows.
Task environments are internet-connected as frozen; any cell with an upstream-fetch signature is recorded, never credited as a delivery or pass mechanism.

gates.thisStudy: This sample answers a variance question, not a benefit question. It cannot merge anything, cannot satisfy the merge gate, and cannot change the predeclared reading or the criterion of the first pair.
gates.merge: PR #212 stays Draft until Simon answers the criterion question recorded in the first pair's outcome.escalation; nothing in this sample decides that question.
gates.hardcodingCheck: The shipped 2.21.0 text is scanned for task-specific material and for the six forbidden host-mechanism names; the pinned test's negative loop enforces the latter.

notes: Why a second sample exists at all: sample 1 measured the same 6,014-byte text at 21 (2026-10-05 window) and 18 (2026-10-06 window) while the candidate read 19 - so the window term (3 cells) was larger than the candidate-minus-control difference (1 cell), and one attempt per cell cannot say whether either number is stable.

What this sample can and cannot do: it can give the window term and the paired difference a second observation each; it cannot manufacture a win, and a favourable reading here would not be read as a gain because the bar and the veto rules are unchanged and are reported alongside.

Both texts were frozen before sample 1 was dispatched and neither was edited since; this sample re-dispatches exactly those bytes, which is why the sample needs no new candidate, no new spec and no new test pin.

criterionDecision.decidedBy: the agent itself, on Simon's 2026-10-07 instruction that the agent decide both the threshold criterion and, if a merge happens, which commit to merge
criterionDecision.criterionKept: The frozen absolute bar stays the merge criterion: strictly more than 21 passes of the 30 predeclared tasks. The same-window paired criterion is NOT adopted as a substitute for it; the paired control keeps exactly the role it was predeclared with, a veto, and this sample is read only under the predeclared rules plus the disclosure below.
criterionDecision.whyNotThePairedCriterion: Sample 1's raw +1 (19 against the same-window control's 18) is not a text effect. On cells where both arms carry a real verdict the pair trades three cells for three, and the whole +1 comes from cells without a real verdict on one side (katex and git-leak-recovery for the candidate against python-statemachine against it). Adopting a criterion at the moment it would convert infrastructure luck into a merge is the exact failure this program's discipline exists to prevent.
criterionDecision.addedDisclosure: Declared before this sample's data exists, and binding on it and on every later reading: a reading is read as a gain only if its win is supported by real verdicts. A candidate that clears the bar only through cells where either arm carries no real verdict (error / not-evaluated / pre-model environment failure) is recorded as an infrastructure-driven reading and is not read as a gain. This is a stricter, disclosed reading of the predeclared bar; the bar and the veto themselves are unchanged.
criterionDecision.mergeTarget: 6539e256 (2.21.0 = main's 6,014-byte text plus the 2.15.0 preservation sentence): its instruction bytes are identical to the measured 48e8aa64, so the merged bytes would equal the measured bytes. It is never merged unless the bar is met.
criterionDecision.ifThisSampleMeetsTheBar: The reading is checked against the unchanged gate (bar met AND same-window veto not triggered AND review ACCEPT AND no hardcoded text) together with this disclosure; if it holds, PR #212's content is replaced by 6539e256 and merged, and the merge record names the reading and the head sha.
criterionDecision.ifThisSampleDoesNotMeetTheBar: The prompt line ends without a merge: PR #212 stays Draft, no further prompt variants are dispatched, and the recorded recommendation is to close the PR rather than merge a text with no measured gain.
criterionDecision.noClaim: No release or efficacy claim is made by this record; it records the agent's own decision under Simon's delegation and does not modify any frozen predeclaration.
